thesis: AI coding assistant pilots stall at renewal because nobody agreed in week one what changed work to measure, so the fix is a one-meeting measurement plan with an owner and a baseline.

anecdotes.summary: Lead story: one fintech team tracked turnaround, other had nothing.
Behind-the-scenes note: author's 2024 pilot with no measurement owner.
Checklist item 6: paper log showed documentation lookups replaced.

claims.statement: In the Northfield Developer Survey 2026 (n=1,240 developers, fielded March 2026), 61% said their company's assistant pilot had "no agreed success measure" at launch.
Among pilots with no success measure, weekly active use fell from 78% in month one to 41% by month three. Among pilots that had one, it fell from 80% to 66%.
Halvorsen Research's 2026 platform team report, built on interviews at 32 companies, found the median pilot ran 94 days before a renewal decision.
Of those 32 companies, 9 tracked any change in cycle time or review load during the pilot. All 9 renewed. Of the 23 that tracked only seat activation, 11 renewed. ... 11 of those 23 still renewed.
A 2025 Ostrava University study of 400 pull requests found no measurable change in review time with assistant use. Some teams that stall are right to stall.
Checklist item 2: Cycle time or review load is what the 9 Halvorsen companies that all renewed were tracking.
Checklist item 5: If the median decision lands at 94 days, a check-in around day 45 gives you time to fix a measurement gap while it still matters.
Checklist item 7: If review time doesn't move, as in the Ostrava study, what's the call?

notes: Day 45 check-in and the 90-day drift phrasing in the checklist are the author's practical advice, not brief figures. Exclusive element for subscribers: the 7-item week-one measurement checklist. A1 (logistics CFO meeting) deliberately left for the long piece.
